audience = the people watching a play, film or concert
performance = a show of music, dance or theatre in front of people
rehearsal = practice before the real show
stage = the raised floor where actors or musicians perform
exhibition = a public show of art or interesting objects
gallery = a building where paintings and art are shown
sculpture = art made by shaping stone, wood or metal
novel = a long written story
author = the person who wrote a book
plot = the main events in a story
character = a person in a book, play or film
chapter = one numbered part of a book
review = an article that says if a film or book is good
live concert = music played in front of an audience, not a recording
lyrics = the words of a song
orchestra = a large group of musicians playing classical instruments
festival = a special event with music, film or food, often over days
tradition = something a community does every year in the same way
carnival = a public celebration with costumes, music and parades
fireworks = explosions of colour in the sky for a celebration
costume = special clothes for a play or celebration
masterpiece = a work of art of the highest quality
classical music = music in the style of Mozart or Chopin, often with an orchestra
science fiction = stories about the future, space or invented science
comedy = a film or play that is meant to make you laugh
horror film = a film that is meant to frighten you
subtitles = words at the bottom of the screen that translate the speech
trailer = a short advert that shows scenes from a new film
box office = the place that sells tickets; how much money a film makes
talent show = a competition where people sing, dance or perform
celebrity = a famous person, often from film or music
museum = a building that shows objects from history, science or art
heritage = history, buildings and traditions passed down from the past
ticket = a piece of paper or code that lets you enter an event
interval = a short break in the middle of a play or concert
bestseller = a book that sells in very large numbers
cinema = a place where you watch films on a large screen
theatre = a building where you watch plays
opera house = a theatre where people sing opera
concert hall = a building designed for music concerts
art gallery = a place that shows paintings and drawings
library book = a book you borrow from a public library
borrow a book = to take a book from a library for a short time
paperback = a book with a soft paper cover
hardback = a book with a stiff cover
e-book = a book you read on a phone, tablet or e-reader
audiobook = a recording of someone reading a book
fairy tale = a traditional story for children, often with magic
short story = a piece of fiction that is shorter than a novel
poem = a piece of writing with rhythm, often in lines
poetry = poems as a type of literature
rhyme = words that end with the same sound
narrator = the person who tells the story
hero = the main good character in a story
villain = the bad character in a story or film
setting = where and when a story happens
twist = a surprising change in a story
ending = the last part of a story or film
page-turner = a book that is so interesting you want to keep reading
bookshelf novel = a novel you keep and display at home
film = a story shown with moving pictures
movie = another word for a film
director = the person who tells actors what to do in a film or play
cast = all the actors in a film or play
leading role = the most important acting part
extra = an actor with no speaking part in a crowd scene
special effects = computer or camera tricks that make impossible things look real
soundtrack = the music in a film
credits = the list of names at the end of a film
blockbuster = a very popular film that makes a lot of money
documentary = a film about real people or facts, not a made-up story
cartoon = a film made from drawings or animation, often for children
soap opera = a TV series about everyday life that continues for years
series = a set of TV programmes with the same characters
episode = one programme in a series
TV season = a group of episodes released together
binge-watch = to watch many episodes in one sitting
channel = a TV station you can choose
remote control = the device you use to change TV channels
on demand = programmes you can start whenever you want
streaming service = a website or app that shows films and series for a fee
playlist = a list of songs you choose to play
hit = a very popular song
album = a collection of songs released together
music single = one song released on its own
band = a group of people who play music together
lead singer = the main singer in a band
guitarist = a person who plays the guitar
drummer = a person who plays the drums
composer = a person who writes music
conductor = the person who leads an orchestra
choir = a group of people who sing together
tune = a series of musical notes that you can remember
beat = the regular pulse of a piece of music
lyrics sheet = a printed copy of the words of a song
pop music = popular music with a strong beat, often for young people
rock music = loud music with guitars and drums
folk music = traditional music of a country or region
jazz = a style of music with improvisation, often with saxophones
hip-hop = a style of music with rap and a strong beat
musical = a play or film in which the actors also sing
ballet = a type of dancing that tells a story with music
play = a story written to be performed by actors on a stage
act = one of the main parts of a play
scene = a short part of a play or film in one place
script = the written words that actors say
curtain = the large cloth that opens and closes on a stage
applause = clapping to show you liked a performance
encore = an extra song or piece after the planned end
standing ovation = when the whole audience stands up and claps
row = a line of seats
aisle seat = a seat next to the walkway in a cinema or theatre
sold-out show = a performance with no tickets left
book tickets = to reserve seats for a film, concert or play
painting = a picture made with paint
drawing = a picture made with pencil, pen or charcoal
portrait = a picture of a person's face
landscape = a picture of the countryside or nature
still life = a picture of objects such as fruit or flowers
sketch = a quick, simple drawing
exhibition opening = the first evening when a new art show is opened
curator = a person who chooses and looks after museum objects
exhibit = an object shown in a museum or gallery
guided visit = a museum tour with someone who explains the exhibits
folk dance = a traditional dance from a region
national costume = traditional clothes of a country
custom = something people in a culture usually do
legend = an old story that may not be completely true
myth = an old story about gods or how the world began
folklore = the traditional stories, songs and beliefs of a place
